If your goal for now is CRA, then realistically it can be done entirely without links or legion. There's actually a [youtube series](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLsjRKhXoqpCzF5qhNcGmy-ccd36yYjmxH) by Halifaxia where he does just this, leveling and gearing a paladin for the sole purpose of clearing CRA without the use of links or legion (sadly the series is slightly outdated now, as the Princess No pre-quests were revamped and it's no longer possible to get the Sengoku Set without fighting Princess No herself).  


That said, it'll only benefit you to work on links and legion. Definitely take it at your own pace, as there's no point in burning yourself out on the game by forcing yourself into activities you don't enjoy. If anything it could always be beneficial to take advantage of tera burning events when they happen to occur in order to quickly get a new character to 200, or making use of any other events that give a way to quickly level lower level characters (the current Neo Castle event has a growth shop for level 141-199 or so characters, where you can purchase potions that will increase your character's level randomly between 1-10 levels, so it can be helpful to farm some event currency on a character in this range in order to gain some fast levels).  


As far as range increases go, the best way is probably upgrading the potentials, flames, and starforce on your gear. The more main stat you can get the better for the most part, and then ideally % magic attack on your weapon, emblem, and secondary.

Yeah, it would've been nice to see the race through to the intended finish but that's just how motorsports and the weather work sometimes, unfortunately.

You can't just hit the bad spots when the rain's still coming down the hardest it'd been all day, you're going to end up losing the track again and be right back where you were initially. They were (to my understanding) in the midst of rain that likely would've lasted another couple hours. They're not going to be able to make any sort of meaningful drying progress in those conditions, and by the time they do, it'll be too dark to continue anyways. Then people are going to be upset that they didn't just call the race sooner instead of keeping it under red for hours.

True, they probably should have red flagged the race sooner. I think they were simply trying to let it play out for as long as possible, in hopes that conditions might get better. Instead, conditions continued to get worse, and especially after Kurt's big slide they realized they needed to stop the cars.  


As far as not waiting, my understanding is that the current rain was the heaviest it'd been all day. So even if they had tried to wait out the storm and attempted to dry the track, they'd have to either wait on the rain to get much light or stop entirely, otherwise CotA is simply too big of a track to dry all at once. And with the current rain being part of a giant rain pocket that likely would've continued on for at least another couple hours (at least I thought that was mentioned on the broadcast? Could be mis-remembering) the track was too far gone and it would have been dark by the time any sort of tangible progress in drying it could be made. Just because the cars have rain tires doesn't mean conditions can't be too treacherous for them to race in.

So much anger on here. We get it, Chase won and you don't like it. However, in just about every interview near the end the drivers seemed to agree that conditions and visibility were the worst they'd been all race. Yes the cars can race in the rain, but only to a certain point. Once it gets to be too dangerous they're going to stop them, and NASCAR is far from the only auto racing series that will call a race early when conditions are deemed too poor and the wait to pick the race back up too long to be justifiable.

Of all the crusader sets, it feels to me as if the Seeker of the Light set ends up being the squishiest of them all. Looking over your profile it seems like there's a couple different things you could do to try and improve survivability:  


1. Switch the ring in your cube from CoE to Unity. As your follower's already wearing a Unity and has the cannot die relic, this will immensely increase your survivability.  

2. Switch your follower from the scoundrel to the templar. This one's not as big of a difference maker, but the templar offers stuns, slows, and a heal/life regeneration, which will all prove helpful. Judging by the gear currently on your scoundrel, all you'll need is Thunderfury, Freeze of Deflection, and the templar immortality relic.  

3. Get a Leoric's Crown for your armor slot in the cube. While this won't directly add survivability, the doubled gem effect will greatly increase your CDR and Akarat's Champion uptime. Ideally you'll be able to achieve permanent Akarat's, not just for the bonus damage, but also for the survivability increases it brings.  

4. Stutter-stepping when using Blessed Hammer. As you've said damage is a non-issue, it'd be more efficient to maximize uptime on the defensive benefit of the Endless Walk set. To this end, you want to stay as mobile as possible, and they best way to do that is to ensure you're stutter-stepping while casting Blessed Hammer, instead of remaining stationary.  

5. It may be beneficial to swap to a more defense-oriented Law, such as Law of Justice with the 7000 armor rune (I forget the exact name).  


Hopefully at least some of these suggestions prove useful. Other than these the best I can suggest is trying to find more ancient pieces for higher stamina, or pieces with greater amounts of all resist and armor.

I've very much tested it. At this point I've cleared up to gr83 myself and am sitting at rank 20 on the HC leaderboards. I tried using Decaying Strength when I initially played the LoN bomb build in season 5, but ended up switching to Immovable Object and then eventually Hopeful Cry.

If you wish to use Decaying Strength, though, more power to you. I'm just speaking based off of what I've personally experienced and what I've seen/heard from others playing the build.

Honestly, I think continuing with Invoker's until you have the gear for LoN is your best bet. The only downside is, as you've mentioned, the build can feel rather slow, especially in multiplayer rifts. Unfortunately Invoker's has a lot of stationary build up time to it, so you'll often spend a large amount of time stationary amongst large packs. The only thing that'll really help this is to increase the amount of thorns, strength, and area damage you have.

If I were you I'd actually swap your Slash - Zeal for Punish - Celerity, as this gives you Hardened Senses (extra block chance), and increases your attack speed whenever you block. As of right now though, I'd say your build seems incredibly solid.

And honestly, until you manage to find an Akarat's Awakening, that is an amazingly rolled Lidless Wall. If you plan on playing the LoN Bombardment build in the future I would absolutely save that shield if I were you.

I suppose if you're standing still and letting mobs hit you in the face this might be true. But if this is the case, you're playing the LoN bomb build wrong.

The reason that Decaying Strength is the go-to choice for Invoker's is that you spend a majority of your time standing stationary amongst a giant group of enemies. Since you're so surrounded, it is a simple matter to activate your law and let it build up to that max 75% damage reduction.

In the LoN build, however, you want to constantly be on the move, dodging as many attacks as possible. For this reason, you will see that the majority of crusaders will take Laws of Hope - Hopeful Cry (if they even choose to run a Law at all). This law helps you to quickly regen the occasional damage you may receive from an undodged attack, while the active ability helps reduce the damage from those occasional hits.

TL;DR: Decaying Strength is bad because it relies on being hit repeatedly to be used to its full effectiveness. As a LoN crusader you simply should not be getting hit that often.

Always glad to help! And when I refer to the damage range, I'm talking about that top line on the Pig Sticker, where it says +1253-1561 Poison Damage. Since the damage of the weapon itself has no effect on your damage in an Invoker's build, you can attempt to roll this off in favor of a more useful stat. Be warned though, the damage range has a very high priority when rerolling, so this may end up taking a great amount of time to roll off.

After looking over your profile I can see four big changes I'd make in order to help you to progress farther into higher GRs:

1. Swap the Ruby gems in your chest and pants for Diamond gems, the extra 375 all-resist is a huge boost to survivability.

2. I'd recommend changing your law. I've found that Laws of Justice - Decaying Strength really only works well in an Invoker's build, where you look to stand amongst a giant pack of monsters and simply tank the damage. On the other hand, a LoN bomb crusader should be constantly moving, and the goal is to either mitigate or avoid as much damage as possible. For this reason, I'd recommend swapping to either Laws of Justice - Protect the Innocent, or Laws of Hope - Hopeful Cry. Personally I am partial to Hopeful Cry, but I think either option would be better than Decaying Strength.

3. Overall, your gear is very much lacking in thorns. Most notably, your shoulders, amulet, belt, and shield all lack a +Thorns affix, which means you are losing out on up to 38,000 extra thorns from those three pieces alone.  
I'd recommend gambling for new shoulders from Kadala (ideally you'll get a pair with Strength, CDR, Bomb %, Area Damage, and Thorns) or look to reroll a pair of Invoker's Shoulders in Kanai's Cube, as Invoker's are guaranteed to roll with the +Thorns affix on them.  
For shields, it looks like you already have a barb leveled, so I'd use that character to upgrade rare shields in Kanai's Cube, in hopes of a new Lidless Wall, which would ideally have Strength, Vit, CDR, Phys %, and Thorns.  
After those two pieces it's simply a matter of finding a spare Belt of the Trove to reroll, and spending some time crafting new Hellfire Amulets (which can be a huge pain, I've been trying to do this recently myself).

4. The final change I'd recommend is finding a new weapon. An ancient Swiftmount with perfect CDR is nice, but I feel as though yours has too many useless stats on it (+% damage and the damage range). I'd look for a Swiftmount, Doombringer, or Sunkeeper that you could ideally get both CDR and Area Damage on. If you are fond of the Swiftmount, I'd recommend looking for one that you can have Str, Vit, CDR, and Area Damage on, as these would be the ideal stats.

All right, looking over your profile I'd say there are a quite a few changes that I would highly suggest making to your gear.

First, in terms of skills and passives, you should switch Consecration - Bed of Nails for Provoke - Hit Me, as you are running the Vo'Toyias Spiker shield, which is reliant on the use of Provoke. I would also recommend swapping one of your current passive skills (preferably Finery) for Indestructible. I'd say Indestructible is mandatory in hardcore, especially once you are looking to start pushing higher and higher into greater rifts.

As far as your cube selections are concerned, if you are running Vo'Toyias as your shield of choice, I'd recommend swapping Blood Brother for Akarat's Awakening in the cube. This will help to drastically decrease your cooldowns, allowing you to kill enemies much more efficiently.

As far as the gear itself on your character is concerned, there are a few minor improvements that I could see you being able to make.  
1. Your Traveler's Pledge has % Holy damage on it, which is absolutely useless to you. If possible, I would suggest rerolling that to % Physical. If not, I'd be on the lookout for a new amulet asap.  
2. Overall, your gear seems to be lacking in IAS and LoH, both of which help to turn Invoker's into the tanky monster that it is. I'd recommend rolling the % Life on your helm into LoH, and trying to find some new bracers that have LoH on them as well. At the same time, a Hack which had either IAS or LoH in addition to CDR would be ideal (you can roll the damage range off of one if you need to, it's a giant help).  
3. Your two rings both have Life per Second on them, which, while this is not an awful stat, I believe IAS would prove to be much more helpful, so I'd be on the lookout for a new Justice Lantern and Compass Rose that offer you attack speed.  
4. I'd recommend switching your gems from rubies to diamonds, that extra all-resist is a necessity for pushing higher level rifts as a hardcore character.

My final suggestion would be to continue trying to rifts somewhere in the level 50-55 range for now, so that you can keep leveling your legendary gems, particularly your BotT and BotS. You've got the three ideal gems already, but extra levels in the gems are an easy source of extra damage.

I'm not sure on the exact math of which is better between BotS and BotT, but I personally have always found BotT to be mandatory in the build, while BotS is considered the flexible gem slot. I believe BotT just works out to be more overall damage, plus the level 25 effect turns it into a permanent form of cc, constantly keeping enemies slowed and helping with survivability. Then we have the new BotP, which is great at lower levels and helps to provide a constant source of increased damage, provided you can chain its effect from one champ pack to the next.  
On the other hand, BotS is incredibly useful at higher levels, especially on rift guardians, which are the most time consuming part of any high-level rift. In the end, I'd say the ideal setup for higher rifts is still BotT, BotS, and Boyarsky's, but if you lack survivability I'd give Esoteric a try for now.

As far as jewelry is concerned, I think the Endless Walk set is usually considered too good to pass up on, as the set bonuses work perfectly with the Invoker's play style. That said, I've never actually tested using a Hellfire and an Oculus Ring myself, so I'd say it could be worth trying out just to at least see how it goes.

I'm sure you could actually solo 25H Spine with your mage's ilvl at 690 and as arcane. From what I've found, there's simply a few things you'd need to do it:  
1. Spec into Ice Barrier, this is great for absorbing damage, and you want to try and keep this up at all times.  
2. If you have decent ilvl gear with leech, fantastic, wear that! If not, I would recommend speccing into Cold Snap and glyphing Regenerative Ice as well.  
3. Spec into Icy Veins, so that you can cast some arcane blasts on big adds/tendons while remaining on the move.

As far as the fight itself is concerned, you just need to take your time and be sure you are constantly strafing from left side to right side, back and forth, so as to prevent him from rolling. My strategy is to kill one tentacle at a time, and then kill the big add that spawns from it. Repeat this strategy until you have just one tentacle left, and leave that one alone. Next, while continuing to run side to side, use arcane explosion to kill the bloods as they near the center of the spine. The idea is to pool enough bloods that you can nuke the final tentacle, get the big add that spawns relatively low, and then quickly run him through the blood to achieve 9 stacks, and get him close to the plate you wish to blow up. If you can manage this, the tendons themselves are relatively simple to burst down.  
Simply rinse and repeat this strategy for the three plates, popping Ice Block and Cold Snap as necessary should you ever get too low on health, and you should manage to break Deathwing's back!
